architect.message: newOOOHeadReadView returns *OOOCompactionHead but silently depends on lastMmapRef==0, which is the only value that makes getOOOSeriesChunks (ooo_head_read.go:114) include the in-memory oooHeadChunk. That contract is not stated, and the series-scan loop is a near copy of NewOOOCompactionHead with different semantics. A later change to the maxMmapRef handling could silently drop the in-memory OOO samples from snapshots. Document that dependency on the type or in the function comment, and keep the test that covers in-memory OOO chunks.

If writeOOOHeadBlocks fails inside Snapshot, the OOO blocks it already wrote (it returns the partial ulids) are left in the snapshot dir, as is the in-order head block. compactOOO now cleans up its partial blocks, but Snapshot ignores the returned ulids, so the two callers handle errors differently. Snapshot holds only cmtx and mtx.RLock, not the head appender lock, so the view's mint/maxt are also a point-in-time scan while appends continue. That is acceptable for a snapshot, but it is worth a comment.

doc-skeptic.message: Comments such as "Append the in-order samples in one commit", "Append the out-of-order samples in a separate commit" and "Create a snapshot and reopen the DB from it" only restate the next lines of code. Only the separate-commit remark carries any why, and it is not stated. Delete them or fold them into one line.
doc-skeptic.suggestion: // In-order and out-of-order samples go in separate commits so the latter land in the OOO head.

lang-go.message: Snapshot's OOO error path returns without removing the OOO blocks already written into dir, while compactOOO (refactored in this same change) removes its partial ULIDs on error. The caller gets an error but the snapshot dir keeps a partial set of blocks. Suggest reusing the same best-effort cleanup of the ULIDs returned by writeOOOHeadBlocks.

newOOOHeadReadView is called with context.Background(), so the O(series) walk over the head cannot be cancelled when the snapshot request is abandoned. Snapshot has no ctx parameter, so this is a hard-coded choice. Consider plumbing a ctx through Snapshot (the callers have one) and passing it here, as compactOOOHead does with NewOOOCompactionHead.

New test TestDB_Snapshot_OutOfOrderHeadNoSideEffects lacks the _AppendV2 suffix. Every sibling test in this V2 file carries it (TestDB_Snapshot_AppendV2 at 528, TestDB_Snapshot_ChunksOutsideOfCompactedRange_AppendV2 at 725, TestDB_SnapshotWithDelete_AppendV2 at 771). Rename to match.

pragmatist.message: newOOOHeadReadView copies about 45 lines of NewOOOCompactionHead (postings walk, per-series locking, min/max tracking) and differs only by skipping the m-map and WBL cut. Two copies of this logic will drift. Consider factoring the shared scan or giving NewOOOCompactionHead a no-mutate mode. The PR description also says the fix uses NewOOOCompactionHead, but the code uses this new function, so the description should be updated.

The existing TestDB_Snapshot_AppendV2 is rewritten into a table-driven test with closures, rather than adding a small separate test as the PR description says (TestDB_Snapshot_WithOutOfOrder_AppendV2, which does not exist in this diff). That makes the diff noisier than needed and hides the original test's intent. Also, the WBL-segment-count assertion in the side-effects test couples to WBL internals. A short separate OOO snapshot test would be simpler to review.

skeptic.message: The new OOO snapshot test only covers one sample that stays in the in-memory OOO head chunk, in a single block range. The other new code paths have no test: m-mapped OOO chunks (the oooMmappedChunks loop in newOOOHeadReadView), OOO data spanning several block ranges (the loop in writeOOOHeadBlocks), and multiple series. A regression in any of them would pass. The side-effects test has 10 in-memory samples and one range too. Add a case with enough OOO samples to force an m-map, and one that spans two block ranges. The non-V2 Snapshot test in db_test.go is also unchanged.

If the OOO block write fails, Snapshot returns an error but leaves the in-order head block and any OOO blocks already written in dir. Callers such as the admin API could then treat a partial snapshot as valid. The refactor now returns the ULIDs written before the failure but Snapshot does not use them to clean up. The same gap existed for the head block, so it is minor, but the new step widens it.

dropped.message: Partial snapshot left in dir when the OOO block write fails.
newOOOHeadReadView is called with context.Background(); plumb a ctx through Snapshot.
TestDB_Snapshot_AppendV2 rewritten table-driven instead of a small separate test; WBL segment count assertion couples to internals.
Test comments restate the next lines of code.

findings.message: When writeOOOHeadBlocks fails, Snapshot returns an error but leaves the in-order head block and any OOO blocks already written in dir. The ULIDs returned on failure are discarded. compactOOO, refactored in this same change, removes its partial blocks on error, so the two callers now handle the same failure differently. The admin API (web/api/v1/api.go:2795) passes the error on and does not clean up dir.

newOOOHeadReadView copies the postings walk and min/max tracking of NewOOOCompactionHead. It also depends on lastMmapRef staying 0, and nothing says so: getOOOSeriesChunks (ooo_head_read.go:114) only includes the in-memory oooHeadChunk when maxMmapRef == 0. If the two copies drift, or someone later sets lastMmapRef here, snapshots could silently lose in-memory OOO samples. Share the scan, or at least document the dependency. The PR description says the fix uses NewOOOCompactionHead, which the code no longer does.

The OOO snapshot cases only cover samples that stay in the in-memory OOO head chunk, in one series and one block range. Two new paths have no test: the oooMmappedChunks loop in newOOOHeadReadView and the per-block-range loop in writeOOOHeadBlocks. A regression in either would still pass. Add a case with enough OOO samples to force an m-map and one whose OOO data spans two block ranges.

TestDB_Snapshot_OutOfOrderHeadNoSideEffects is the only test in this file without an AppendV2/AppenderV2 marker. Its siblings are TestDB_Snapshot_AppendV2 (528), TestDB_Snapshot_ChunksOutsideOfCompactedRange_AppendV2 (725) and TestDB_SnapshotWithDelete_AppendV2 (771). The PR description also names a test, TestDB_Snapshot_WithOutOfOrder_AppendV2, that does not exist in the diff.
